title: Repositories: where packages come from
summary: The files that list your repositories on Debian and Rocky, and how to ask apt and dnf what they would do.

text: apt reads /etc/apt/sources.list and /etc/apt/sources.list.d/. Debian 13's new format: one block per repository.
- URIs: the server. Suites: the release and its updates. Components: parts of the archive.
- Security updates have their own server and suite. man sources.list explains every field.
dnf reads .repo files in /etc/yum.repos.d/, one [section] per repository. The real file uses mirrorlist= (a list of mirrors), with baseurl commented out.
- dnf fills in $releasever and $basearch: 9 and x86_64, for example.
- Paths are case-sensitive: BaseOS, not baseos.
- gpgcheck=1 checks every package's signature: keep it on.
Before you install, ask: nothing changes, and you learn what would happen.
- apt policy shows the installed version, the candidate (what apt install would get) and the repository it comes from.
- dnf --repo=NAME uses only that repository, for this one command. --disablerepo and --enablerepo work too, without editing any file.
